- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the overshoot at +3% above the 14-day moving average to prevent overbought bias.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 2–3 days, shift forecast horizon slightly backward (e.g., 1–2 days) for short-term (1–7 day) horizons.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 65% of the 18-day moving average, apply a downward bias correction of 0.5–1.5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5) and forecast is erratic, smooth the forecast curve using a 5-day moving average to reduce noise.
